title: Christopher Nolan Bans Ugg Boots From His Sets, Calls Them a 'Signifier of Modernity'
excerpt: The Odyssey director explained his infamous no-Uggs rule on CBS Mornings, tracing it back to Emily Blunt's sheepskin rebellion during Oppenheimer.
body:
• Christopher Nolan has confirmed he bans Ugg boots from his film sets, calling them a "signifier of modernity" that breaks the immersive atmosphere he builds for actors.
  • The director explained the rule on CBS Mornings while promoting The Odyssey, saying even small anachronisms can "weirdly take you out of reality."
  • The ban became a running joke during Oppenheimer, when Emily Blunt repeatedly wore Uggs on set and received "withering looks" from Nolan — then gifted him a pair as a wrap present.
  • Anne Hathaway first revealed the policy on Brittany Broski's Royal Court podcast while promoting The Odyssey alongside co-star Matt Damon.

Christopher Nolan's filmmaking demands are legendary — practical explosions over CGI, 70mm IMAX film over digital, and entire scripts written without a computer. But the Oscar-winning director's most talked-about rule this week has nothing to do with cameras or visual effects. It's about footwear.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Voilg_VDAbU

Appearing on CBS Mornings on Monday to promote The Odyssey, Nolan was asked by host Gayle King about reports that he bans Ugg boots from his sets. The question followed Anne Hathaway's recent revelation on Brittany Broski's Royal Court podcast: "Chris says no Uggs on the set."

The Method Behind the Boot Ban

Nolan laughed before offering a characteristically thoughtful explanation. "It's a joke I have with Emily Blunt, and Anne before then," he said. "Sometimes actors will turn up, because the footwear hurts them, so they'll turn up in these big fluffy comfy slippers."

He compared the effect to someone eating a bag of chips off-camera — a tiny intrusion of the mundane into a carefully constructed fictional world. "There are just certain things that remind you you're in the real world as opposed to the world we're trying to create for the actors," he said. "I want to stay in the moment. And so for me, Ugg boots are a signifier of modernity."

Emily Blunt and the Origin Story

The Ugg controversy first surfaced during Oppenheimer, when Emily Blunt — playing Kitty Oppenheimer — repeatedly swapped her uncomfortable 1940s-era shoes for sheepskin boots between takes.

"You can be on a set where you've got a guy holding a microphone, you've got a giant camera, you've got crew everywhere. But something like that can actually weirdly take you out of reality."

— Christopher Nolan, on CBS Mornings

"I've never known anyone to detest a pair of Uggs more than Chris Nolan," Blunt told USA Today in 2023. "I would sometimes put on some Uggs and I'd just get this withering look down to my feet — it was like being in The Devil Wears Prada again."

On The View that same year, Nolan said Blunt "used to drive me crazy" wearing the boots instead of period-appropriate footwear. "I'd immediately say to her, 'Can you please just get rid of the boots, put the shoes on, and get ready to go?'"

Blunt had the last laugh. As a wrap gift after Oppenheimer, she gave Nolan a pair of Ugg slippers — a move his wife and producer Emma Thomas called "brilliant." Nolan admitted they were "pretty comfortable."

Nolan's Broader War on Modern Distractions

The Ugg ban fits a wider pattern. Nolan famously operates without a cell phone, email, or text messages. When he wanted Matt Damon for The Odyssey, his wife texted Damon first to arrange a call — from a random landline at Universal Studios.

Even Nolan, Damon added, "doesn't know what number it's going to be."

""There are just certain things that remind you you're in the real world as opposed to the world we're trying to create for the actors," he said."

On set, this philosophy means every detail serves the story. For The Odyssey — shot entirely on IMAX 70mm film with practical effects — Nolan built real ancient Greek sets, filmed in remote caves and on open water, and demanded his cast remain in character even off-camera.

The Odyssey opened on July 17 and features Damon as Odysseus, Hathaway as Penelope, Tom Holland as Telemachus, Zendaya as Athena, and Robert Pattinson as Antinous. The film premiered in Mumbai earlier this month — a nod to India's growing theatrical market that Nolan has championed since Tenet.

When King suggested Nolan simply had a personal grudge against Uggs, he was quick to clarify. "No, Uggs are great," he said. Just not on his set.
